title: A 28-day menstrual cycle
body: Riya, aged 16, keeps a diary of her menstrual cycle, which lasts 28 days. Menstrual flow occurs from day 1 to day 5. Over the next days, a follicle in one of her ovaries grows and the lining of her uterus becomes thicker again. Near the middle of the cycle the levels of two pituitary hormones rise to a peak and a mature follicle ruptures. After this, the remaining part of the ruptured follicle changes into a yellowish body that secretes a hormone. If no fertilisation takes place, this body degenerates and the next menstrual flow begins on day 29, which becomes day 1 of a new cycle. Her biology teacher reminds the class that the cycle is controlled by pituitary and ovarian hormones, and that hygiene during menstruation is very important.
